articles.title: Enchanted
articles.summary: Glossy surface with scattered bright flake specks catching light, like glitter dust under clearcoat in whatever colour you give it. A glossy paint in your colour with a soft hint of green-tinged shimmer; the blotches barely show, so it reads as a clean gloss with a little mystery.
articles.what: Up close: Takes your colour: the paint is a flat placeholder grey with faint pale-green smudges, 6-20 px, scattered thinly. The spec strips show low base metal with irregular bright metal blotches (small slanted smudges) and clearcoat at full gloss with a few dark spots; no regular flake grid. From a distance: A glossy paint in your colour with a soft hint of green-tinged shimmer; the blotches barely show, so it reads as a clean gloss with a little mystery. Measured spec (average): metal 49, roughness 42, coat 16. Shine: high gloss. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, roof.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, stock car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Enchanted on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: metal blotches read best on large flat gloss panels
Whole body: a clean, quiet gloss base
Numbers read cleanly in their own colour on a gloss base; no interference.
Almost any pattern, stripes or graphics: the low-key gloss carries them
Pairs well with: solid gloss black, chrome trim, white stripes.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not heavy glitter flake: the old card says bright flake specks, the strips show only a few metal blotches (sparkle 9)
Not green paint: the green is a faint smudge on a grey placeholder, the colour is yours
Avoid: small numbers get lost in the flake, next to matte finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 49 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 42 (high gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: small numbers get lost in the flake, next to matte finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost any pattern, stripes or graphics: the low-key gloss carries them; carbon or hex: stays clean
Patterns to avoid: other flake or glitter patterns: it adds its own, redundant
Spec overlays that work: metal flake: add real sparkle, the base is subtle; matte stripe: contrast band against the high gloss
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
